fix.subject: workqueue: Fix false positive stall reports
fix.author: Song Liu
fix.landed_on: v6.16-fb (Meta cherry-pick D97801303 of upstream 8fce6de954cb; the upstream copy c7f27a8ab9f2 is in linus-upstream and v7.1-fb)

signature_match_evidence: The changelog describes false workqueue-watchdog stall reports on weakly ordered arm64: wq_watchdog_timer_fn's lockless check sees a non-empty worklist next to a stale last_progress_ts. This MID is the Meta panic_on_wq_watchdog BUG hit inside wq_watchdog_timer_fn (kernel BUG at kernel/workqueue.c:7558, softirq on call_on_irq_stack). It fires only on arm64 (Grace/armv9). Sample dmesg: 'BUG: workqueue lockup - pool cpus=1 ... nice=-20 stuck for 796s!', then 'Showing busy workqueues and worker pools:' prints nothing for the stalled pool before the BUG. So the pool was not actually busy, which is a false positive. A 6.13 sample shows the same thing: 'curr 0 (swapper/12) ... stuck for 203s' on an idle CPU. Omar's [META] debugging commits under the same task add that 'by the time show_cpu_pool_hog() is called the stall has cleared itself'.
gt_root_cause: In wq_watchdog_timer_fn() the pool->worklist emptiness and pool->last_progress_ts (watchdog_ts) are read without pool->lock. On arm64 the watchdog CPU can see the list_add from insert_work() in __queue_work() before it sees the matching last_progress_ts = jiffies store. If the pool had been idle for a long time, the stale timestamp makes the pool look stuck for hundreds of seconds. With Meta's panic-on-wq-stall this becomes a BUG(). The fix re-reads last_progress_ts under pool->lock before declaring a stall.
family_label: workqueue watchdog false-positive stall (arm64 memory reordering)
fair_test_rationale: The raw crash only shows the watchdog BUG with a long 'stuck for Ns' value and an empty or absent busy-pool listing. To reach the answer you have to notice the stalled pool is idle, see that the lockless timestamp/worklist check in wq_watchdog_timer_fn can be reordered on arm64, and propose re-checking under pool->lock. The fix commit is not named or hinted at in the crash output.

problems: Minor: 8fce6de954cb (the cherry-pick source named in the commit trailer) is not on any release or upstream branch in this mirror, only on scratch/personal branches. The upstream copy that did land is c7f27a8ab9f2, which is on linus-upstream and v7.1-fb. The case already says this, so calling 8fce6de954cb 'upstream' is only a small wording slip.
Not checked: I did not re-read the dmesg quotes (empty busy-pool listing, arm64-only, the 6.13 sample). I only confirmed the MID/category via Hive and the commit content via git.

fix.subject: timers/migration: Fix livelock in tmigr_handle_remote_up()
fix.author: Amit Matityahu
fix.landed_on: v7.1-fb, linus-upstream (stable copies: 07b3b83587fb in linux-6.12.y / ust v6.12.94+-fb, 1d6c2062b77b in linux-6.18.y / ust v6.18.36+-fb)

signature_match_evidence: The changelog describes an endless goto-again loop in tmigr_handle_remote_up(): tmigr_handle_remote_cpu() skips timer_expire_remote() when cpu == smp_processor_id(), so the same expired event keeps coming back. The fleet crash is 'watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#N stuck for 22s! [ksoftirqd/N]' with the stack run_timer_softirq -> tmigr_handle_remote -> __walk_groups -> tmigr_handle_remote_up -> tmigr_handle_remote_cpu. In one sample (twshared4075.29.lla2) the RIP is tmigr_handle_remote+0x232, and the code bytes (mov %gs:cpu_number,%eax; cmp %ebp,%eax; je skip; call timer_expire_remote) are exactly the 'if (cpu != smp_processor_id()) timer_expire_remote(cpu)' check the fix removes. The goto-again loop at timer_migration.c:1030/1033 is the only loop that can keep one softirq invocation running for more than 20 seconds.
gt_root_cause: jiffies can advance after the local CPU has run its BASE_GLOBAL timers in run_timer_base() and before tmigr_handle_remote() looks at the migration hierarchy. A local global timer that becomes expired in that window then shows up as an expired event for the local CPU. tmigr_handle_remote_cpu() skips timer_expire_remote() for the local CPU, so the timer is never run or removed. fetch_next_timer_interrupt_remote() keeps reporting it as expired, the event is requeued with expires == now, and tmigr_handle_remote_up() spins in its goto-again loop in softirq context, which triggers the soft lockup. The fix calls timer_expire_remote() unconditionally.
family_label: timer migration hierarchy livelock in tmigr_handle_remote_up
mechanism_class: livelock / race between jiffies advance and remote timer handling
fair_test_rationale: The crash only shows a softirq soft lockup inside the tmigr remote-handling walk. To find the cause you have to read tmigr_handle_remote_up() and tmigr_handle_remote_cpu(), notice that the local CPU's expiry is skipped while jiffies may have moved on, and see that this requeues the same event forever. The crash does not mention the fix, and the crashing kernel (6.9) predates it.

problems: Minor: signature evidence cites the goto-again loop at timer_migration.c:1030/1033. In crash kernel 28f2d09ad102 the 'again:' label is at line 1012 and 'goto again' is at line 1033. The skipped check 'if (cpu != smp_processor_id()) timer_expire_remote(cpu);' is at lines 937-938. None of this changes the verdict.

fix.author: Amit Matityahu
fix.landed_on: v7.1-fb, linus-upstream (stable copies: 07b3b83587fb in linux-6.12.y, 1d6c2062b77b in linux-6.18.y)

signature_match_evidence: Soft lockup in hardirq-exit softirq with RIP in __walk_groups (+0x1e6 / +0x32b; tmigr_handle_remote_up is inlined into it). gt_root_cause: When jiffies advances between the local CPU's own global-timer expiry and the tmigr remote-handling pass, the local CPU's expired event stays in the hierarchy. tmigr_handle_remote_cpu() skips timer_expire_remote() for smp_processor_id(), so the timer is never run and is requeued as expired. tmigr_handle_remote_up() then loops through goto again indefinitely, and the watchdog reports a soft lockup. family_label: timer migration hierarchy livelock in tmigr_handle_remote_up
mechanism_class: livelock / race between jiffies advance and remote timer handling
fair_test_rationale: The crash shows a soft lockup inside __walk_groups/tmigr_handle_remote_up with no reference to the fix. Finding the cause requires working out that the local-CPU skip in tmigr_handle_remote_cpu() combined with a jiffies race produces an event that never gets consumed. The crashing kernel does not contain the fix (verified with merge-base).

fix.subject: sched/mmcid: Don't assume CID is CPU owned on mode switch
fix.author: Thomas Gleixner
fix.landed_on: v6.19-fb (v6.19-fbk0-rc10+, release-v6.19-fbk705); cherry-pick of upstream 1e83ccd5921a (also on v7.1-fb)

signature_match_evidence: Oops is a write page fault (error_code 0x3) at RIP sched_mm_cid_exit+0x1ea, on a locked btr (clear_bit). The symbolized backtrace reads mm_drop_cid <- mm_drop_cid_on_cpu <- sched_mm_cid_exit <- do_exit, and RDX=0x2000001d is a CID with MM_CID_TRANSIT (bit 29) set. That matches the changelog: sched_mm_cid_exit() assumes the CID is CPU-owned, calls mm_drop_cid_on_cpu(), and then clear_bit() gets a huge bit number because TRANSIT is set. The same page-fault oops shows up on 7 hosts across 6.19.0 fbk0 rc4/rc6/rc7/rc8, and none of those kernels contain 5757c00b91b5 or upstream 1e83ccd5921a. No hits on later 6.19 kernels that have the fix.
gt_root_cause: While in per-CPU CID mode, the fixup sets MM_CID_TRANSIT on a task that is running in userspace. That task then exits without being scheduled again. sched_mm_cid_exit() sees that the previous mode was per-CPU and assumes the CID is CPU-owned, so it calls mm_drop_cid_on_cpu(). That clears an ONCPU bit that was never set and runs clear_bit(cid) with the TRANSIT bit (bit 29) still in the value, an out-of-bounds atomic bit clear far past the mm cid bitmap. The fix checks that the CID really is CPU-owned before dropping it.
family_label: mmcid-transit-cid-oob-clear-bit-on-exit
mechanism_class: out-of-bounds bit operation (bad CID state on mode switch)
fair_test_rationale: The crash shows only sched_mm_cid_exit/mm_drop_cid_on_cpu and a register value with bit 29 set. To get to the fix you have to decode the TRANSIT flag, see that the CID is not CPU-owned, and find the 6.19-fb backport. The crash kernel lacks both the backport and the upstream commit.

fix.subject: sched_ext: Fix incorrect sched_class settings for per-cpu migration tasks
fix.author: Zqiang
fix.landed_on: v6.13-fb (release-v6.13-fbk13 and later, through fbk18); cherry-pick of upstream 1dd6c84f1c54

signature_match_evidence: kernel BUG at kernel/sched/rt.c:1035 in dequeue_rt_stack, from dequeue_task_rt <- schedule <- smpboot_thread_fn. The task is always Comm: migration/N (the per-CPU stopper), and the crash comes right after 'sched_ext: BPF scheduler ... enabled'. The changelog says that loading a BPF scheduler runs __setscheduler_class() over scx_tasks, which wrongly gives the per-CPU migration (stop-class) tasks rt_sched_class. When the stopper later sleeps, the RT dequeue path trips the BUG_ON. Across 6.13 kernels this MID shows up on every build without b1e6e0777cbd (fbk5 to fbk12, hundreds of hosts). It is absent from every build with the fix (fbk13 02230262e956, fbk14, fbk15, fbk16, fbk17). The 6.16 builds behave the same way with the 6.16 backport.
gt_root_cause: When a sched_ext scheduler is enabled, scx_enable walks every task and calls __setscheduler_class(). For the per-CPU migration/stopper kthreads (stop_sched_class) this returns rt_sched_class, so their sched_class becomes RT while they are actually queued and handled as stop tasks. When migration/N blocks in smpboot_thread_fn, dequeue_task_rt()/dequeue_rt_stack() runs on an rt_se that was never enqueued on an rt_rq, and the BUG_ON in rt.c fires. The fix adds scx_setscheduler_class(), which keeps stop_sched_class tasks unchanged.
family_label: scx-enable-migration-thread-gets-rt-class
mechanism_class: wrong sched_class assignment (state corruption on class switch)
fair_test_rationale: The crash shows only an RT-class BUG in dequeue_rt_stack for a migration/N thread after a BPF scheduler was enabled. The fix is in sched_ext's class-switch code, and its changelog describes a misclassification with no crash signature, so the link has to be reasoned out. The crash kernel lacks both b1e6e0777cbd and upstream 1dd6c84f1c54.

problems: Minor: rt.c:1035 in the crash kernel (0b66b3635210) is BUG_ON(!rq->nr_running) in dequeue_top_rt_rq(), which is inlined into dequeue_rt_stack(). It is not a BUG_ON placed directly in dequeue_rt_stack.

Unverified: the claim that 6.16 builds carry 'the 6.16 backport'. Neither b1e6e0777cbd nor 1dd6c84f1c54 is an ancestor of refs/heads/v6.16-fb, so any 6.16 backport would have a different SHA. I did not check this.

Branch-landing detail confirmed: b1e6e0777cbd is on refs/heads/v6.13-fb (first tag v6.13-fbk13). Upstream 1dd6c84f1c54 is on linus-upstream, main and v6.19-fb. Neither commit is an ancestor of the crash kernel 0b66b3635210 (fbk12).

fix.subject: FBONLY: sched/fair: clamp rescaled vlag in reweight_entity() to bound entity_key()
fix.author: Rik van Riel
fix.landed_on: v6.13-fb (release-v6.13-fbk17, fbk18); the same patch as fa191eb086a7 is on release-v6.13-fbk16 (v6.13-fbk16 GA/hotfixes); upstream-equivalent on v6.16-fb 22ec93f3948c and v7.1-fb ccd3bc00e3e5

signature_match_evidence: The panic is an RCU stall with every CPU spinning on the rq lock in sched_balance_rq() (from sched_balance_newidle/pick_next_task_fair). All 17 fbk16-rc1 samples first log 'WARNING at kernel/sched/fair.c:691 __enqueue_entity', which is the WARN_ON_ONCE((w_vruntime >> 63) != (w_vruntime >> 62)) overflow guard in __sum_w_vruntime_add(). That is exactly the changelog's sequence: the overflow guard trips, avg_vruntime and rb-tree state become corrupt, and the load balancer wedges with every CPU spinning in sched_balance_rq(). Crash kernel 242a742712f1 contains 'Increase weight bits for avg_vruntime' (3f374515315d) but not the clamp. The MID is almost entirely confined to this kernel (17 of 20 hosts) and does not appear on fbk16 GA or fbk17, which carry the clamp.
gt_root_cause: reweight_entity() rescales vlag by old_weight/new_weight and never re-clamps it. On a large weight drop for a deep group sched_entity (update_cfs_group), se->vruntime drifts far below zero_vruntime. The next __enqueue_entity() then computes entity_key*weight, which overflows s64 (made reachable by 'Increase weight bits for avg_vruntime'). That corrupts sum_w_vruntime and the rb-tree ordering, the load balancer livelocks on rq locks, and the result is an RCU stall or hard lockup. The fix clamps vlag to the entity_lag() bound after installing the new weight.
family_label: eevdf-reweight-vlag-overflow-balance-lockup
mechanism_class: integer overflow corrupting runqueue accounting leading to lockup
fair_test_rationale: The raw crash is a generic rq-lock RCU stall in the load balancer. The only hint is an earlier overflow WARN in __enqueue_entity, and it points at the enqueue path, not at reweight_entity(). Connecting it to the missing vlag clamp takes EEVDF reasoning. The crash kernel lacks both 54262cda76de and fa191eb086a7.

problems: Minor: the other 3 of the 20 hosts run 6.16.1-0_fbk2 (f40efc324cc8, hardened/hotfix2/hotfix3). Those kernels also lack the v6.16-fb equivalent fix 22ec93f3948c, which supports the case rather than weakening it.

Not independently checked: the claim that each fbk16-rc1 sample first logs 'WARNING at kernel/sched/fair.c:691 __enqueue_entity'. The narrow Hive query returns only hostname, time, kernel and category_key.

fix.subject: btrfs: fix block group refcount race in btrfs_create_pending_block_groups()

fix.landed_on: v6.13-fb (release-v6.13-fbk9 onward); landed with the 5-patch bg_list refcount series (04845e5b3332 harden bg_list against list_del races, 30cb23135cee discard_workfn explicit ref, 34edad068624, 221243213b29). An earlier landing (54d2e767c643) was reverted on 2025-11-07.

fix.author: Leo Martins
fix.landed_on: v7.1-fb (release-v7.1-fbk0, release-v7.1-fbk1); upstream 5eff4d5b17fa

signature_match_evidence: 'kernel BUG at fs/btrfs/extent_map.c:83' comes from btrfs_free_extent_map called by btrfs_scan_inode in the extent map shrinker. This is the META-ONLY debug trap (61507d9da57a) that BUG()s when an extent_map is freed while still on a list/tree. The fix changelog: split maps inherit EXTENT_FLAG_LOGGING, 'when it is freed while still on the inode's modified_extents list (for example by the extent map shrinker) it trips the WARN_ON(!list_empty(&em->list)) in btrfs_free_extent_map()'. subsystem: btrfs extent_map / tree-log / extent map shrinker

fix.subject: mm: fix the race between collapse and PT_RECLAIM under per-vma lock
fix.author: Barry Song
fix.landed_on: v6.16-fb (v6.16-fbk7); cherry-pick 40a5b5c12a28 on release-v6.16-fbk6 (v6.16-fbk6-rc4, v6.16-fbk6, -hotfix1/2)

signature_match_evidence: The backport 81edd93d2ee4 (per-VMA lock for MADV_DONTNEED) entered fbk6. Kernel fbk6-rc2 (c6774c13965a) has it but does not have the collapse/PT_RECLAIM fix. The next rc, fbk6-rc4, was built at 40a5b5c12a28, which is this fix. Only one other commit sits between rc2 and rc4, a sched_ext warning change. 196 of this MID's 197 hosts are on rc2. The sample shows 'BUG: Bad page map' with pte f000eef3f000eef3 and pmd:00000067, meaning the PMD points at freed/zeroed physical page 0, i.e. a freed page table. It then oopses in unmap_page_range via zap_page_range_single_batched<-madvise (process_madvise), which is the per-VMA-lock MADV_DONTNEED path named in the changelog.
gt_root_cause: With MADV_DONTNEED running under the per-VMA lock, PT_RECLAIM can free an empty PTE page. khugepaged's collapse only checked check_pmd_still_valid() under mmap_lock and did not take vma_start_write() first. So collapse and PT_RECLAIM race, a page table gets freed or reused while still reachable, and later zaps walk garbage PMDs/PTEs. The fix calls vma_start_write() before check_pmd_still_valid().
family_label: khugepaged collapse vs PT_RECLAIM page-table UAF under per-VMA lock
fair_test_rationale: The crash shows only corrupted PTEs/PMDs in the zap path. Neither khugepaged nor PT_RECLAIM appears, so the solver has to connect the corruption to the new per-VMA-lock DONTNEED path and its race with collapse.

problems: Minor: the changelog's example oops goes through exit_mmap->unmap_vmas->unmap_page_range, not the madvise path. The mechanism is the same (a freed page table walked in unmap_page_range after the collapse vs PT_RECLAIM race), so the match still holds, but the claim that the call trace 'matches the changelog' is loose.
Minor: the fix only moves vma_start_write(vma) earlier in mm/khugepaged.c (a 1-line move, from after check_pmd_still_valid() to before it). That is consistent with the stated root cause.

fix.subject: flexfiles/pNFS: fix NULL checks on result of ff_layout_choose_ds_for_read
fix.author: Tigran Mkrtchyan
fix.landed_on: v6.16-fb (v6.16-fbk7-rc0 and later); upstream 5a46d2339a5a

signature_match_evidence: Oops: NULL deref at address 0x30, RIP ff_layout_pg_init_read+0x446 [nfs_layout_flexfiles], reached from nfs_file_direct_read (pread64) while dmesg shows 'nfs: server ... not responding'. Code bytes show mirror = FF_LAYOUT_COMP(lseg, ds_idx). RDX (ds_idx) = 0x7f23 is uninitialized stack garbage (it looks like the upper half of a user address), so the idx >= mirror_array_cnt check returns a NULL mirror and the next load mirror->mirror_ds faults. This is the path the fix closes: after backport 262b304751fa, ff_layout_choose_ds_for_read() returns ERR_PTR, but ff_layout_pg_init_read still checks 'if (!ds)', so it goes on with an unset ds_idx. The fix changes these checks to IS_ERR(ds). Sibling MID 63912f4e7929 (readahead path, 16 hosts) has the same cause.
gt_root_cause: The v6.16-fb backport of 'pNFS/flexfiles: don't attempt pnfs on fatal DS errors' (262b304751fa) made ff_layout_choose_ds_for_read() return ERR_PTR(-EINVAL/-EAGAIN) instead of NULL. When every DS mirror is unavailable (for example the DS is not responding), the error pointer is treated as a valid DS and best_idx is never written. ff_layout_pg_init_read then indexes the mirror array with an uninitialized ds_idx, gets a NULL mirror and dereferences mirror->mirror_ds, oopsing at 0x30.

mechanism_class: NULL/ERR_PTR check mismatch -> uninitialized index -> NULL deref
fair_test_rationale: The crash shows only a NULL deref inside ff_layout_pg_init_read during pread/readahead, with DS-not-responding messages nearby. To reach the fix you have to disassemble the function, see that the mirror index is uninitialized, and trace it back to the ERR_PTR-vs-NULL change in the flexfiles DS-selection helpers. Nothing in the raw crash names the fix commit or the error-pointer change.

I checked the base commit 0e127f210adc and it lacks the fix (4fff4aafa348 is not an ancestor) while containing the regressing backport 262b304751fa. fix.subject: fuse: revert back to __readahead_folio() for readahead
fix.author: Joanne Koong
fix.landed_on: v6.13-fb (v6.13-fbk10+; also 2e4fa9e95b01 on the v6.13-fbk9 release line); upstream 0c67c37e1710

signature_match_evidence: Oops (NULL write at 0x8, an LRU list_del with dead000000000122 in RDX) in __folio_put, called from fuse_copy_page <- fuse_copy_args <- fuse_dev_do_write <- fuse_dev_splice_write, comm fuse_worker. This is a folio put while the folio is still on the LRU, i.e. its refcount was dropped too early in the splice page-move path (fuse_try_move_folio inlined into fuse_copy_page). The changelog says exactly this: readahead_folio() drops the folio reference, but the splice path that swaps page-cache folios assumes ap->folios still holds one, causing a UAF. Timeline supports it: every crashing 6.13 kernel (fbk5-fbk8, fbk9-rc0 401b6bba80f5) lacks the fix, crashes stop around 2025-11-20 after it landed, and only 1 host crashed on fbk9 (b487e362c3df, which has 2e4fa9e95b01). Sibling MIDs ad4d32bbdf84 (do_splice) and eb525dd3fd5e/e80c94b7ed6f (free_pcppages_bulk from fuse_copy_page) look the same.
gt_root_cause: Commit 3eab9d7bc2f4 converted fuse_readahead to readahead_folio(), which drops the folio reference once the folio is locked. The splice reply path (fuse_dev_splice_write -> fuse_copy_page -> fuse_try_move_folio) replaces the page-cache folio and then calls folio_put(oldfolio), assuming ap->folios[] holds its own reference. Without that reference, the put releases the page cache's reference: the folio is freed while still on the LRU and in use, and __folio_put crashes on LRU list corruption. Going back to __readahead_folio() keeps a reference for the life of the readpages request.
family_label: fuse-readahead-splice-folio-refcount-uaf
fair_test_rationale: The stack is a splice write from the FUSE daemon crashing in __folio_put; readahead does not appear at all. To connect it to the readahead_folio() conversion you have to reason about where the ap->folios references come from, which is what the fix addresses. The fix sha is not visible in the crash.

problems: Minor: the claim that crashes stop around 2025-11-20 is too loose. Hosts on fbk9-rc0 (401b6bba80f5), which lacks the fix, kept crashing through 2025-12-02 (e.g. time 1764718552). That still fits the fix being the cure, but the evidence text should say 'stop on fixed kernels', not 'stop by date'.

fix.subject: blk-cgroup: add cond_resched() in blkg_async_bio_workfn
fix.author: Chris Mason
fix.landed_on: v6.9-fb (v6.9-fbk12+); cherry-picked to v6.16-fb (cdf915018eb6), v6.19-fb (9a7faac24f41), v7.1-fb (41e77cf14101), and merged into v6.13-fb via f83f7a3e2a29

signature_match_evidence: 'watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#82 stuck for 22s! [kworker/u897:13]', Workqueue: blkcg_punt_bio blkg_async_bio_workfn, RIP blkg_async_bio_workfn+0xb5, on a dm_crypt OCI host. fix.subject: block: integrity: Do not call set_page_dirty_lock()
fix.author: Martin K. Petersen

signature_match_evidence: Oops (page fault at 0x1070) in folio_mark_dirty <- set_page_dirty_lock <- bio_integrity_unpin_bvec <- bio_integrity_unmap_user <- blkdev_bio_end_io <- blk_mq_end_request_batch <- nvme_irq, i.e. in hard-IRQ context on direct I/O with user PI buffers; nvme protection errors appear just before. The changelog says: 'Placing multiple protection information buffers inside the same page can lead to oopses because set_page_dirty_lock() can't be called from interrupt context', and the fix drops the call. Sibling MIDs on the same kernel (797cb9985ebb unpin_user_page, b4aeed67d90c, f8c55cdd9c35, 5d4a1c0b1edf) come from the same unpin path. The crash kernel commit 98c4aee38d77 does not contain f978ab261997.
gt_root_cause: bio_integrity_map_user (from 492c5d455969 'directly map user buffers') pins user PI/metadata pages, and on read completion bio_integrity_unpin_bvec(dirty=true) calls set_page_dirty_lock(). For block-device direct I/O the completion runs from the NVMe interrupt (blk_mq_end_request_batch -> blkdev_bio_end_io), so set_page_dirty_lock/folio_mark_dirty run in IRQ context on user pages, possibly with several PI buffers sharing a page. They take the folio lock and touch mapping state, which is unsafe there and oopses. PI buffers are not file-backed, so the fix simply stops dirtying them.
family_label: blk-integrity-set_page_dirty_lock-in-irq
fair_test_rationale: The stack clearly shows set_page_dirty_lock called from bio_integrity_unpin_bvec in nvme_irq context, so the idea of not dirtying PI pages is fairly guessable. A solver still has to say why it is wrong (IRQ context, PI buffers not file-backed) instead of blaming a bad folio or mapping. Caveat: the crash kernel is a 6.11 ublk zero-copy scratch build (scratch/sruffell) deployed on twstorage hosts, not a mainline release kernel. The fix commit is not named in the crash.

fix.subject: cgroup: avoid null de-ref in css_rstat_exit()
fix.author: JP Kobryn
fix.landed_on: v6.16-fb (first in v6.16-fbk3, also release-v6.16-fbk4/fbk5); upstream original eea51c6e3f66 (v6.17-rc2)

signature_match_evidence: The oops is inside css_rstat_flush(), inlined css_rstat_updated_list at rstat.c:290 'if (!rstatc->updated_next)' with rstatc = css_rstat_cpu(css, cpu). It is called from css_rstat_exit()+0x23 in css_free_rwork_fn on the cgroup_destroy workqueue. x86 shows 'BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address 0000000000000020'. The same dmesg shows a WARNING at rstat.c:308 and SLUB 'Unable to allocate memory' just before, which is the css_create() error path (percpu_ref_init, cgroup_idr_alloc or css_rstat_init failing) queueing css_free_rwork_fn while css->rstat_cpu is still NULL. gt_root_cause: When css_create() fails after init_and_link_css(), e.g. a percpu_ref_init, cgroup_idr_alloc or css_rstat_init allocation failure under memory pressure, its error path queues css_free_rwork_fn. fair_test_rationale: The crash shows a NULL deref in css_rstat_flush called from css_rstat_exit on the cgroup_destroy workqueue, plus a nearby allocation failure. signature_match_evidence: Panic is 'kernel BUG at fs/btrfs/extent-io-tree.c:572!'. In the crash kernel 66649fefaca1, line 572 is BUG_ON(ret < 0) after add_extent_changeset() in clear_state_bit(). The fix changelog says __btrfs_qgroup_release_data() passes a changeset whose add_extent_changeset() calls ulist_add(GFP_ATOMIC) under the io-tree spinlock and 'If this allocation fails, it hits a BUG_ON and panics the kernel'. The fix skips the ulist allocation for bytes-only callers, so the BUG_ON can no longer be reached.

fair_test_rationale: The crash shows only a BUG_ON line number and a qgroup release stack. To connect it to the fix, you have to map extent-io-tree.c:572 to add_extent_changeset's -ENOMEM from GFP_ATOMIC ulist_add, and then see that the callers only need bytes_changed. The fix was made later by a human engineer, and the crash text does not name it.

fix.subject: btrfs: fix discard worker infinite loop after disabling discard

To solve it you have to reason out the specific loop: a used block group stuck on the unused discard list while discard is disabled or the fs is RO, so __add_to_discard_list becomes a no-op and peek_discard_list returns the same group every time. fix.subject: blk-rq-qos: fix crash on rq_qos_wait vs. rq_qos_wake_function race

fix.landed_on: linus-upstream (v6.12-rc4); also on v6.13-fb/v6.16-fb, backported to v6.9-fb as f98e304782ff; never picked into v6.11-fb

signature_match_evidence: Crash: 'BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: 0000000000034fa0' (and 0000000100035fb0) in wake_up_process <- rq_qos_wake_function <- __wake_up <- wbt_done, i.e. a fault while taking p->pi_lock (queued_spin_lock_slowpath). The fix changelog shows the same mechanism: a page fault in raw_spin_lock_irqsave(&p->pi_lock) inside try_to_wake_up <- rq_qos_wake_function <- __wake_up (from the wbt path). The cause is that data->task sits on the waiter's stack in rq_qos_wait(). The waiter sees got_token after the waker's list_del_init, returns, and overwrites that stack slot before the waker calls wake_up_process(data->task).
production_validation: Since 2025-10-06 this MID shows up only on 6.11 kernels (231406f0162e 253, 562def7b21ed 6, ccdaeca790c6 1). That whole branch lacks the fix, including the newest 6.11 build 562def7b21ed (2026-04-30); merge-base --is-ancestor is false for both 231406f0162e and 562def7b21ed. The newer-kernel storage population is small, so this validation is moderate.
gt_root_cause: rq_qos_wait() keeps its wait entry and the rq_qos_wait_data (including data->task) on its own stack. rq_qos_wake_function() does: set data->got_token, list_del_init(&curr->entry), then wake_up_process(data->task). Between the list_del_init and the wake_up_process, the waiter can see got_token, skip sleeping, return from rq_qos_wait and reuse its stack. The waker then passes a garbage task pointer to try_to_wake_up() and faults on p->pi_lock. The fix takes a reference on the task and reads data->task before list_del_init, so the waker never touches the waiter's stack after it can return.

fair_test_rationale: The crash names rq_qos_wake_function and wbt_done, but not the fix. fix.landed_on: release-v6.16-fbk6 (the 6.16-fbk6 release line; cherry-pick of upstream 366a4532d96f, v6.17-rc2)

signature_match_evidence: Crash: 'BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffea05a1ffe2c8' in unmap_page_range <- zap_page_range_single_batched <- madvise_vma_behavior <- process_madvise, which is the MADV_DONTNEED zap path. fbk6-rc1/rc2 were the first 6.16 builds with the backport of 'mm: use per_vma lock for MADV_DONTNEED' (81edd93d2ee4); it is absent from fbk5 0e127f210adc. That change lets madvise_dontneed and PT_RECLAIM run under only the per-VMA lock. The fix changelog says khugepaged collapse's check_pmd_still_valid() is protected only by mmap_lock, so it races with PT_RECLAIM under the per-VMA lock and walks freed or changed page tables in unmap_page_range. The fix moves vma_start_write() ahead of the check. The only commits between rc2 (c6774c13965a) and rc4 (40a5b5c12a28) are this fix and one sched_ext warning change.
production_validation: On 6.16 the MID appears only on fbk6_rc2 (197 crashes, about 7% of that kernel's 2805 crashes) and fbk6_rc1 (1). It ran steadily from 2026-07-29 to 2026-08-18 and then stopped. Kernels that contain 40a5b5c12a28 (fbk6 rc4/rc5/rc6/rc8 and final 8fc89c59249c incl. hotfix1/hotfix2/hardened) logged about 9,200 crashes of other MIDs through 2026-09-30 and 0 of this MID. fbk5 is not affected because it lacks the per-VMA MADV_DONTNEED backport. The handful of older 6.13 hits (5, all with different fault addresses) are unrelated noise.
gt_root_cause: The 6.16-fbk6 backport of per-VMA-lock MADV_DONTNEED (a6fde7add78d) let madvise_dontneed, and with it PT_RECLAIM's freeing of empty PTE tables, run with only the per-VMA read lock. khugepaged's collapse_huge_page() still called check_pmd_still_valid() before vma_start_write(), relying only on mmap_lock held for write. Collapse and PT_RECLAIM could then change or free the same PMD/PTE table at once, and zap_page_range_single_batched -> unmap_page_range dereferenced a stale page-table entry or page. The fix calls vma_start_write() before check_pmd_still_valid(), so collapse excludes per-VMA-lock madvise.
family_label: per-VMA-lock MADV_DONTNEED/PT_RECLAIM races khugepaged collapse -> bad page-table walk in zap
fair_test_rationale: The crash stack is entirely on the madvise/zap side and never mentions khugepaged, collapse or PT_RECLAIM, and the fix only changes mm/khugepaged.c. A solver has to connect the new per-VMA-lock MADV_DONTNEED backport in the fbk6 rc to a missing exclusion in collapse, which the raw crash does not suggest. The production data is a clean before/after split: the MID disappears exactly at the rc that adds the fix.

It is presumably the upstream original. The backport actually in rc2, and absent from fbk5 0e127f210adc, is 81edd93d2ee4, which signature_match_evidence names correctly.
Minor: the 6.13 hits are 5 in total (2 on fbk6-hotfix3 and 3 on fbk5), which matches the stated count. They are old noise, as claimed. I did not independently check the fault addresses.

fix.subject: bpf: Fix remap of arena.
fix.author: Alexei Starovoitov
fix.landed_on: linus-upstream (v6.10-rc6); contained in v6.11-fb and later; never picked into v6.9-fb

signature_match_evidence: Crash: 'BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000008' (also 0x0) in arena_vm_close <- exit_mmap <- __mmput <- do_exit. The crash kernel's arena_vm_close() unconditionally does list_del(&vml->head); kfree(vml). It has no arena_vm_open() and no vml->mmap_count, so a VMA duplicated by fork, mremap or split shares one vml, and the second close runs list_del on freed memory. On hardened/init_on_free kernels that memory is zeroed, which gives the write to NULL+8 or NULL. The fix changelog: 'The bpf arena logic didn't account for mremap operation. Add a refcnt for multiple mmap events to prevent use-after-free in arena_vm_close.' It adds arena_vm_open() and an mmap_count refcount, and kfrees vml only on the last close.
production_validation: The MID appears only on 6.9 kernels (28f2d09ad102 hardened 548, 28f2d09ad102 159, 4304beb4596b 30, plus brcmrdma/c5fa564d33e3 variants) and never on 6.11/6.13/6.16, which all contain the fix. Validation is limited: hosts that hit the MID almost never ran newer kernels (5864 crashes on 6.9, 2 on 6.16, 0 of this MID on 6.16).
gt_root_cause: The original bpf_arena mmap support kept one vma_list entry (vml) per mmap in vma->vm_private_data. It had no vm_ops->open, so a copied VMA (from fork, mremap or split) shared the same vml with no refcount. When the copies were torn down (e.g. exit_mmap), the first arena_vm_close() did list_del and kfree(vml), and the next one did list_del on the freed or zeroed vml, causing a use-after-free or NULL dereference. The fix adds arena_vm_open(), which bumps a refcount, and frees the vml only when the refcount drops to zero.
family_label: bpf arena vma_list entry shared across duplicated VMAs without refcount -> UAF in arena_vm_close
fair_test_rationale: The stack points at kernel/bpf/arena.c, but a solver still has to notice that the 6.9 tree has no vm_ops->open or refcount for the per-VMA vml, and that VMA duplication (fork/mremap/split) leads to a double teardown. The fix's subject ('Fix remap of arena.') describes mremap rather than the exit_mmap NULL dereference, so it does not match the crash signature on its face. It is missing from the crash kernel's release branch (v6.9-fb).

problems: The 'never picked into v6.9-fb' part of landed_on is imprecise. A backport, 47facbb63d0e ('bpf: Fix remap of arena.', Aug 2024), sits on refs/heads/v6.9-fb_old and on a branch literally named origin/v6.9-fb. Other copies are 87496a1b01e8 on stable/linux-6.9.y and 8c0d4ceacfc6 on the chantra backport branch. None of them is on the current refs/heads/v6.9-fb. The sample crash kernel 28f2d09ad102 (on v6.9-fb) lacks both b90d77e5fd78 and 47facbb63d0e, as do 4304beb4596b (release-v6.9-fbk13) and c5fa564d33e3 (fbk10). So crash_kernel_lacks_fix still holds, but the landing note should say 'dropped from, or never in, the current v6.9-fb lineage'.

Minor point: the evidence mentions the fork/split path, but the fix changelog only names mremap. In the crash kernel the arena VMA gets VM_DONTEXPAND and not VM_DONTCOPY, so fork does duplicate it and share one vml with no refcount. The mechanism is consistent with the exit_mmap stack.
Not independently checked: the exact oops addresses (0x8/0x0) in the raw dmesg, and the per-kernel counts in production_validation.

fix.subject: btrfs: fix subvolume deletion lockup caused by inodes xarray race
fix.author: Omar Sandoval
fix.landed_on: refs/heads/v6.13-fb (v6.13-fbk7+); v6.11-fb equivalent 1ec7ad3bd548 (v6.11-fbk14+); upstream f6a6c280059c / e7f1c0265894

signature_match_evidence: Changelog says that if an inode is left out of root->inodes by the evict()/btrfs_iget() race, btrfs_add_dead_root() runs too early, and btrfs_clean_one_deleted_snapshot() -> btrfs_kill_all_delayed_nodes() then loops forever because the delayed_nodes xarray never empties. It adds 'We saw this manifest as soft lockups in production.' The MID is a soft lockup whose top frames are btrfs_kill_all_delayed_nodes <- btrfs_clean_one_deleted_snapshot <- cleaner_kthread, which is exactly that path.
production_validation: On 6.13.2 builds the MID hit only fbk5 and fbk6 (111 crashes); both lack the fix. 6.13 fbk7-fbk18, which have it, logged about 290k crashes of other MIDs and 0 of this one. On 6.11.1 the MID hit fbk12 and fbk13 (37 crashes; neither has the fix). 6.11 fbk14-16, which have 1ec7ad3bd548, logged about 5.9k other crashes and 0 of this one.
gt_root_cause: There is a window in evict() between remove_inode_hash() and btrfs_del_inode_from_root(). If btrfs_iget() recreates the same inode in that window, the new inode goes into root->inodes, and eviction then erases that new entry with a plain __xa_erase. The live inode is now missing from the xarray. When the other inodes are evicted the root looks empty, so it is queued as a dead root too early. Because the lost inode still holds a delayed_node, btrfs_kill_all_delayed_nodes() spins forever in the cleaner thread. The fix only erases the xarray entry if it still points to this inode (__xa_cmpxchg).
family_label: btrfs subvolume-deletion cleaner soft lockup from inode xarray eviction race
fair_test_rationale: The crash only shows a soft lockup in btrfs_kill_all_delayed_nodes from the cleaner kthread. To get the root cause you have to see why the delayed_nodes xarray never empties: an inode is missing from root->inodes because of an evict/iget race in btrfs_del_inode_from_root(), a function the stack never mentions. Nothing in the raw crash names the fix.

problems: Minor: e7f1c0265894 is not on linus-upstream. It is the btrfs-tree original that 4dfcd888c6ee was cherry-picked from, and in this mirror it is reachable only from non-release branches such as v6.13-fb_old and user/scratch branches. The upstream mainline commit is f6a6c280059c, so the 'upstream f6a6c280059c / e7f1c0265894' label should name f6a6c280059c alone.
Minor: the fix is co-authored by Leo Martins (Co-authored-by and Signed-off-by lines), not by Omar Sandoval alone. Both are human.

fix.subject: bpf: Fix for use-after-free bug in inline_bpf_loop
fix.author: Eduard Zingerman
fix.landed_on: refs/heads/v5.12-fb (merged via 8a17ec0b5815 by Andrii Nakryiko; in release-v5.12-fbk16); upstream fb4e3b33e3e7

signature_match_evidence: The oops is in inline_bpf_loop, called from bpf_check during BPF_PROG_LOAD. The crash kernel's inline_bpf_loop() calls new_prog = bpf_patch_insn_data(...) and then writes env->prog->insnsi[call_insn_offset].imm = callback_offset. The changelog names exactly this pattern: bpf_patch_insn_data() may free env->prog, so the later write through env->prog is a use-after-free.
production_validation: The MID logged 1175 crashes on 5.12 fbk9 (b6cf154957d9 and its hotfix5), which lack the fix. 5.12 fbk16 builds (eb00762ce6d2), which contain fc454ace7eb0, logged 392 crashes of other MIDs and 0 of this one. This is weak evidence: no fboss hosts ran fbk16 in the window, so the affected workload was never actually tested on a fixed kernel.
gt_root_cause: When the verifier inlines bpf_loop, bpf_patch_insn_data() can reallocate the program and free the old env->prog. inline_bpf_loop() then patches the callback offset through the stale env->prog pointer (env->prog->insnsi[...].imm) instead of new_prog. That use-after-free write/read oopses during program load. The fix writes through new_prog->insnsi.
family_label: BPF verifier bpf_loop inlining use-after-free of env->prog
fair_test_rationale: The crash frame names inline_bpf_loop but gives no hint that bpf_patch_insn_data() reallocates the prog or that env->prog is stale. Finding that means reading the function and knowing the patching semantics. The fix lives on the internal v5.12-fb branch, and nothing in the crash names it.

problems: Minor: the fix's commit_date 2023-05-02 is the committer date from Andrii Nakryiko's cherry-pick. The author date is 2022-06-24. Nothing needs correcting.

Minor: production validation is weak, as the case already says, because no fboss hosts ran a fixed fbk16 kernel. The code-level evidence does confirm the case: the buggy line is in the crash kernel and the fix is not an ancestor of it.

fix.subject: flexfiles/pNFS: fix NULL checks on result of ff_layout_choose_ds_for_read
fix.author: Tigran Mkrtchyan
fix.landed_on: refs/heads/v6.16-fb (v6.16-fbk7+); upstream 5a46d2339a5a

signature_match_evidence: Every crash is 'BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000030' in ff_layout_pg_init_read. The crash kernel has 262b304751fa (backport of f06bedfa62d5), which changed ff_layout_choose_ds_for_read() to return ERR_PTR, but ff_layout_pg_init_read still tests 'if (!ds)'. An ERR_PTR therefore passes the check, and the code uses an uninitialised ds_idx in mirror = FF_LAYOUT_COMP(lseg, ds_idx) followed by mirror->mirror_ds->... In the crash kernel's struct nfs4_ff_layout_mirror, mirror_ds sits at offset 0x30 (layout 8, mirrors 16, ds_count+efficiency 8, devid 16), which matches the faulting address for a NULL mirror. The fix changes these checks to IS_ERR(ds).
production_validation: All 138 crashes were on 6.16 fbk3, fbk4 and fbk5 builds. They came in bursts, e.g. many hosts at 1788318416, which fits a data-server outage. fbk6 (8fc89c59249c) also lacks the fix; it logged about 8.6k other crashes and 0 of this MID, so that says little. Only fbk7-rc builds contain the fix (about 236 crashes of other MIDs, 0 of this one). Validation is weak because the fixed kernels are barely deployed.
gt_root_cause: Commit f06bedfa62d5 ('pNFS/flexfiles: don't attempt pnfs on fatal DS errors') made ff_layout_choose_ds_for_read() return ERR_PTR instead of NULL on failure, but the callers still tested for NULL. When no data server is usable, ff_layout_pg_init_read accepts the error pointer as a valid DS and indexes the mirror array with an uninitialised ds_idx. It then dereferences a NULL or garbage mirror (mirror->mirror_ds at +0x30) instead of falling back to the MDS or retrying.

fair_test_rationale: The raw crash only shows a NULL dereference at +0x30 in ff_layout_pg_init_read. To solve it you have to see that a backported upstream change switched the return convention of ff_layout_choose_ds_for_read() to ERR_PTR while its callers kept NULL checks, and map offset 0x30 to mirror->mirror_ds. fix.subject: mm/list_lru: break long lock hold times in __list_lru_walk_one()
fix.author: Danielle Costantino
fix.landed_on: refs/heads/v6.13-fb (v6.13-fbk15+)

signature_match_evidence: Changelog: 'prevents soft lockups caused by extreme spinlock contention on the per-memcg list_lru_one lock during inode cache shrinking... on KVM guests under severe memory pressure when kswapd walks an LRU list with millions of inodes. The virt_spin_lock (test-and-set)... vCPU preemption of the lock holder extends the effective lock hold time... triggering soft lockups across dozens of CPUs spinning on the same lock.' This MID is a soft lockup on KVM guests (devvm*) in queued_spin_lock_slowpath under list_lru_add_obj <- iput. That CPU is waiting for the same per-memcg list_lru_one lock held by the long __list_lru_walk_one() walk. 100 of the 131 hosts also hit the sibling MID b357dccd57bf2c9cede05324f3d7dc44 (a waiter in prune_icache_sb), which the fix commit cites by name.
production_validation: All 178 crashes were on 6.13 fbk7 devvm kernels (bc14455e13aa and its hotfixes), which lack the fix. The devvm fleet did not move to fbk15+ during the window (devvm crashes on fbk9+ total about 3), so there is no before/after comparison.
gt_root_cause: __list_lru_walk_one(), called from prune_icache_sb/super_cache_scan via kswapd or the shrinker, holds the per-memcg list_lru_one spinlock across very long walks of inode LRUs with millions of entries and never drops it. On KVM guests the unfair test-and-set virt_spin_lock and vCPU preemption of the lock holder stretch the hold time to seconds. Many other CPUs spin on the same lock and hit soft lockups; here that is iput -> list_lru_add_obj during dentry shrinking. The fix adds a need_resched() check that drops the lock, reschedules and restarts the walk.
family_label: list_lru_one lock hold-time soft lockups on KVM guests during inode shrinking
mechanism_class: lock contention / long lock hold (soft lockup)
fair_test_rationale: The crash shows a victim CPU spinning in list_lru_add_obj. The lock holder, a long __list_lru_walk_one() under the shrinker, is not in the stack. Reaching the fix means inferring the holder, the lack of a resched point in the LRU walk, and the KVM virt_spin_lock unfairness. The fix commit names a different MID, not this one.

problems: Minor: the Signed-off-by line reads 'Daniel Costantino <dcostantino@meta.com>', but the author field is 'Danielle Costantino <dcostantino@fb.com>'. It is still a human author, so this is cosmetic only.

fix.subject: btrfs: fix block group refcount race in btrfs_create_pending_block_groups()
fix.author: Boris Burkov
fix.landed_on: refs/heads/v6.13-fb (v6.13-fbk9+, with the rest of Boris's bg_list refcount series 04845e5b3332/34edad068624/30cb23135cee/221243213b29); upstream 2d8e5168d48a (already in 6.16 base)

signature_match_evidence: The oops happens when btrfs_delete_unused_bgs(), run from btrfs_reclaim_bgs_work, passes a block group taken from the unused_bgs list to btrfs_discard_queue_work(). Faults are NULL/garbage derefs (0x223, 0x8, 0x711318), which fits a freed or reused btrfs_block_group. The changelog describes a race between btrfs_create_pending_block_groups (list_del_init + clear_bit BLOCK_GROUP_FLAG_NEW without unused_bg_lock) and btrfs_mark_bg_unused (list_move_tail). That race breaks the block group refcount, the group is freed early, and btrfs_delete_unused_bgs keeps using it. The changelog adds that it 'is most likely to happen after a relocation finishes which cancels discard, tears down the block group', i.e. the reclaim/relocation plus unused-bg-deletion plus discard path in this stack.
production_validation: On 6.13 the MID hit only fbk5 through fbk8 (147 crashes, the last on fbk5-hotfix2 at 1781222782). All of these lack the series. v6.13-fbk9 is the first build with the fix, and fbk9-fbk18 logged about 290k crashes of other MIDs and 0 of this one. 6.16 builds already carry the upstream fix 2d8e5168d48a and show 0 crashes of this MID.
gt_root_cause: A block group is linked into space_info by btrfs_make_block_group() before btrfs_create_pending_block_groups() finishes creating it. btrfs_create_pending_block_groups() then did list_del_init(&bg->bg_list) and clear_bit(BLOCK_GROUP_FLAG_NEW) without holding fs_info->unused_bgs_lock. A concurrent btrfs_mark_bg_unused() could see a non-empty list with the NEW bit still set and list_move_tail the group onto unused_bgs without taking a reference. The refcount then hits zero one put early, and btrfs_delete_unused_bgs (from reclaim) later uses the freed block group; here it crashes inside btrfs_discard_queue_work. The fix does the list_del_init and clear_bit under unused_bgs_lock so the two happen atomically.
family_label: btrfs block group bg_list refcount race causing use-after-free in unused-bg deletion/discard
fair_test_rationale: The crash only shows a bad pointer inside btrfs_discard_queue_work during unused block group deletion. The root cause is a missing lock in a different function (btrfs_create_pending_block_groups) that desynchronises bg_list membership and the refcount, and neither that function nor the fix appears in the crash. Caveat: the fix is one of five bg_list refcount patches that landed together between fbk8 and fbk9, and its changelog shows the resulting refcount underflow warning rather than this exact oops.

problems: Minor caveat, already noted in the case: the changelog's example trace is a refcount_t underflow WARNING in btrfs_discard_workfn -> btrfs_put_block_group -> btrfs_discard_cancel_work. That is not this oops in btrfs_discard_queue_work under btrfs_delete_unused_bgs/btrfs_reclaim_bgs_work. The link to this crash is a mechanism-level inference plus the production A/B evidence, not an exact trace match.
Fix 03630ddf2fba is one of several bg_list refcount patches that landed together in v6.13-fbk9, so the per-commit attribution cannot be separated using production data alone.

fix.subject: spi: tegra210-quad: Protect curr_xfer check in IRQ handler

fix.subject: btrfs: fix subvolume deletion lockup caused by inodes xarray race

signature_match_evidence: The crash is a soft lockup (45-63s) in btrfs-cleaner at btrfs_kill_all_delayed_nodes <- btrfs_clean_one_deleted_snapshot. The changelog says a lost inode with a delayed_node makes btrfs_kill_all_delayed_nodes() 'loop forever because the delayed_nodes xarray will never become empty ... We saw this manifest as soft lockups in production.' Upstream is e7f1c0265894; the v6.11-fb backport is 1ec7ad3bd548.
production_validation: On v6.13, crashes came from fbk5 (347) and fbk6 (513), which lack the fix. fbk7 (bc14455e13aa) and later contain it: 2 crashes in this category out of 272,906 crashes of any kind on 6.13 fbk7-fbk19. If btrfs_iget() recreates the same inode in that window, the new entry is added to the xarray and then erased by the old inode's eviction. The cleaner's btrfs_kill_all_delayed_nodes() then spins forever because the lost inode's delayed_node keeps root->delayed_nodes non-empty. fair_test_rationale: The crash only shows a soft lockup in the cleaner's delayed-node teardown. Finding the cause means working back to an unrelated evict()/btrfs_iget() race on the root->inodes xarray, which appears nowhere in the stack. The fix is a human-authored upstream fix (Omar Sandoval / Leo Martins, Meta), and production data shows the MID stops when it lands.

fix.subject: sched_ext: Fix incorrect sched_class settings for per-cpu migration tasks
fix.author: Zqiang

signature_match_evidence: The panic is 'kernel BUG at kernel/sched/rt.c:1035!', which is BUG_ON(!rq->nr_running) in dequeue_top_rt_rq(), reached via dequeue_task_rt from schedule() in smpboot_thread_fn. The only smpboot threads normally scheduled as RT/stop are the per-CPU migration (stopper) threads. The changelog shows that loading a sched_ext scheduler switches migration/N tasks to rt_sched_class and leaves them there after unload, so a stop-class task gets dequeued through the RT class. Upstream is 1dd6c84f1c54; the v6.16-fb backport is 35eb4fdb72a0.

fix.subject: bpf: Fix remap of arena.
fix.author: Alexei Starovoitov
fix.landed_on: linus-upstream

signature_match_evidence: The panics are GPFs in arena_vm_close during exit_mmap at non-canonical 0xdead000000000108 (LIST_POISON1+8, so list_del on an already-deleted vma_list) and 0x2d78756e696c2d6c (freed, reused memory). In the crash kernel, arena_vm_close() does list_del()+kfree() of vma->vm_private_data with no .open callback and no refcount, and arena_map_mmap sets no VM_DONTCOPY. A duplicated VMA (fork or mremap) therefore shares one vml that gets closed twice. The fix adds arena_vm_open and an mmap_count refcount 'to prevent use-after-free in arena_vm_close'.
production_validation: The arena_vm_close category appears only on 6.9 kernels (5,000+ crashes). v6.9-fb never received b90d77e5fd78, while v6.11-fb and v6.13-fb contain it. Kernels 6.11/6.13/6.16/6.19 had 0 arena_vm_close crashes but 544,221 crashes of other kinds since 2026-02-05, when this MID started.

When the arena VMA is duplicated (mremap copy_vma, or fork since VM_DONTCOPY is not set), both VMAs share the same struct vma_list in vm_private_data. Each arena_vm_close() then does list_del(&vml->head) and kfree(vml), giving a double list_del (LIST_POISON GPF) and use-after-free at process exit. fair_test_rationale: The crash shows only a GPF in arena_vm_close at exit. The solver must work out that VMA duplication makes vm_private_data shared and freed twice. The fix changelog frames it around mremap and the subject does not mention close or exit. The fix is upstream, human-authored and never backported to v6.9-fb. fix.subject: btrfs: fix block group refcount race in btrfs_create_pending_block_groups()
fix.author: Boris Burkov

signature_match_evidence: The crash is a NULL deref (addr 0x8, list pointer) in remove_from_discard_list <- btrfs_discard_cancel_work <- btrfs_delete_unused_bgs from reclaim work, i.e. using a block group whose refcount was already dropped. The changelog describes a btrfs_create_pending_block_groups vs btrfs_mark_bg_unused race that breaks bg_list refcounting ('refcount_t: underflow; use-after-free' in btrfs_discard_cancel_work) and notes it 'is most likely to happen after a relocation finishes which cancels discard, tears down the block group'. Upstream is 2d8e5168d48a. It landed as a series with 04845e5b3332 ('harden block_group::bg_list against list_del() races', which describes the btrfs_delete_unused_bgs interleaving), 30cb23135cee, 34edad068624 and 221243213b29.
production_validation: The 7 btrfs_delete_unused_bgs MIDs (this one plus bcbbb3b2, 53cf41f8, e4c8d9d0, 0a1f5be9, 975a6d52, 24211aca) had 3,403 crashes on fbk8-hotfix1, 3,070 on fbk6-hotfix3, and so on. These 5 btrfs commits are the only fs/btrfs changes between 8695f611147d and v6.13-fbk9. 6.13 fbk9-fbk19 (all contain the fix) had 0 btrfs_delete_unused_bgs crashes out of 219,791 crashes on 119,849 hosts. 6.16/6.19 (fix upstream) had 0 out of 204,051.
gt_root_cause: btrfs_create_pending_block_groups() does list_del_init(bg_list) and clears BLOCK_GROUP_FLAG_NEW without holding unused_bgs_lock. A concurrent btrfs_mark_bg_unused() can see the list non-empty and the NEW bit set, then list_move_tail the bg onto unused_bgs without taking a reference. The bg_list refcount ends up off by one. btrfs_delete_unused_bgs (from auto-reclaim) then drops the final reference early and later touches the freed block group: discard list, free-space ctl lock, rb tree. The fix makes list_del_init + clear_bit atomic under the lock, and the series makes bg_list refcounting explicit and uniform.
family_label: btrfs-block-group-bg_list-refcount-race-uaf
fair_test_rationale: The crash shows a UAF-like NULL deref in the unused block group deletion/discard path. The root cause is a list/flag race in block group creation (btrfs_create_pending_block_groups), which is not on the stack. The fix is a human-authored upstream series backported by Meta. The whole family of 7 MIDs disappears on kernels containing it, with this series as the only btrfs delta.

fix.subject: btrfs: avoid GFP_ATOMIC allocations in qgroup release/free paths
fix.author: Leo Martins
fix.landed_on: refs/heads/v6.13-fb (first in v6.13-fbk15; the equivalent pick 113ee43707a0 is in fbk14 final 894401a424c9; upstream variant e0a85137a882 on linus-upstream)

signature_match_evidence: The panic reads 'kernel BUG at fs/btrfs/extent-io-tree.c:584!'. In 0b66b3635210 and 02230262e956, line 584 is the BUG_ON(ret < 0) that follows add_extent_changeset() in clear_state_bit(). The stack is __clear_extent_bit <- alloc_ordered_extent, which is where the qgroup release/free is inlined. The changelog says exactly this: add_extent_changeset() calls ulist_add(GFP_ATOMIC) under the io-tree spinlock from __btrfs_qgroup_release_data/qgroup_free_reserved_data, and 'If this allocation fails, it hits a BUG_ON and panics the kernel'.
production_validation: All 294 crashes of this MID are on kernels without the fix: fbk12 0b66b3635210 (+hotfix1/2), fbk13 02230262e956 (+hotfix1), fbk14_rc0 and fbk14_rc1 (both lack it). gt_root_cause: BLOCK_GROUP_FLAG_NEW handling in btrfs_create_pending_block_groups did list_del_init + clear_bit without holding unused_bgs_lock. A concurrent btrfs_mark_bg_unused could see the list non-empty and the NEW bit still set, and list_move_tail the bg onto unused_bgs without taking a reference. btrfs_delete_unused_bgs then drops a reference it never owned. The block group is freed while still reachable, which is a use-after-free and list corruption in the unused/reclaim worker. The fix takes the lock around list_del_init+clear_bit and makes all bg_list refcounting uniform.
family_label: btrfs block_group bg_list refcount race -> UAF in delete_unused_bgs
fair_test_rationale: The crash is a bare GPF in the unused-bg deletion worker with a garbage address. Nothing in it points to the bg-creation path or unused_bgs_lock. To find the fix you have to suspect a refcount underflow from racing bg_list users.

problems: Minor: the fix is one of 5 btrfs patches that landed together between v6.13-fbk8 and fbk9, so production data alone cannot show whether 03630ddf2fba or its companion 04845e5b3332 (bg_list list_del hardening) stops this crash. The case already says this in landed_on, and 03630ddf2fba is the root-cause patch the series is named after.

fix.subject: bpf: Fix remap of arena.
fix.author: Alexei Starovoitov
fix.landed_on: refs/heads/linus-upstream (v6.10). It is present in v6.11-fb/v6.13-fb/v6.16-fb but never backported to v6.9-fb. The follow-up hardening 4fddde2a732d 'bpf: Fix use-after-free in arena_vm_close on fork' (2026-04-15, upstream) adds VM_DONTCOPY/may_split/mremap rejection.

signature_match_evidence: The GPF address is 0xdead000000000108, i.e. LIST_POISON1+8, in arena_vm_close. That means list_del on a vma_list entry that was already deleted and freed. The v6.9-fb arena_vm_ops has only .close/.fault and no .open refcount, so any duplicated VMA (fork, split, mremap) shares one vml and closes it twice. The changelog: 'Add a refcnt for multiple mmap events to prevent use-after-free in arena_vm_close.' Here the second close comes from munmap inside mmap_region (MAP_FIXED over the arena), by task BpfJailerIO0.
production_validation: There are 4,148 arena_vm_close crashes since 2026-07 (burst from 2026-07-27, when a BpfJailer rollout started). All are on 6.9.0 kernels (fbk2-fbk13), which lack b90d77e5. There are 0 on 6.11/6.13/6.16 kernels, which include it through v6.10. Caveat: this commit predates the crash kernel. It is a fix the 6.9-fb branch never picked up, not a later landing.
gt_root_cause: The bpf_arena mmap code on 6.9 keeps one vma_list per mmap in vm_private_data and has no vm_ops->open. When a VMA is duplicated (fork/dup, split, or mremap copy_vma), both VMAs share the same vml. Each arena_vm_close does list_del+kfree on it: that is a double list_del and double kfree, i.e. a use-after-free. The upstream fix adds arena_vm_open with a mmap_count refcount, so the vml is removed and freed only on the last close.
family_label: bpf arena shared vma_list double close (missing vm_open refcount)
fair_test_rationale: The crash names arena_vm_close and shows a list-poison address. The solver still has to notice that 6.9's arena_vm_ops has no open/refcount, and connect munmap-from-mmap_region to a duplicated VMA. The fix subject ('Fix remap of arena') does not match the mmap/munmap signature on its face.

problems: Minor: the fix b90d77e5 (2024-06-18) predates the crash kernel. It is a missing backport on v6.9-fb, not a later-landed fix. The case already says this.
I did not re-read the raw oops text, so the 0xdead000000000108 address and the BpfJailerIO0 task name are taken from the case as given.

fix.subject: bpf: Fix remap of arena.
fix.author: Alexei Starovoitov
fix.landed_on: refs/heads/linus-upstream (v6.10). Present in v6.11-fb and later, absent from v6.9-fb.

signature_match_evidence: The GPF is at 0xdead000000000132, which is LIST_POISON2 (0x...122) plus 0x10, in __kmalloc_node from __vmalloc_node_range (the vm pages array for a 16K thread stack: 4 pointers, 32 bytes, so kmalloc-32). The 24-byte arena struct vma_list also lives in kmalloc-32, and the SLUB free pointer offset there is 16, which is where list_del writes LIST_POISON2. So a double arena_vm_close list_del that hits a freed kmalloc-32 object turns the freelist pointer into 0xdead...122, and the next allocation dereferences +0x10. This is a downstream symptom of the same arena double close. Inference: the crash stack never mentions bpf arena. The link rests on the poison arithmetic and the fleet correlation below.
production_validation: This MID started 2026-07-27 17:10, within an hour of the arena_vm_close MID (cce36956, 2026-07-27 16:07). Both occur only on 6.9.0 kernels, and 208 hosts hit both signatures. There are 0 crashes on 6.11/6.13/6.16 kernels, which contain b90d77e5.
gt_root_cause: The bpf arena on 6.9 has no vm_open refcount, so duplicated VMAs share one vma_list. The second arena_vm_close does list_del+kfree on an already-freed kmalloc-32 object. list_del writes LIST_POISON2 over the SLUB freelist pointer at offset 16, which corrupts the kmalloc-32 freelist. The next kmalloc-32 allocation, here the vmalloc pages array for a new thread stack in clone3, follows the poisoned pointer and faults at 0xdead000000000132.
family_label: bpf arena shared vma_list double close (missing vm_open refcount) -> kmalloc-32 freelist corruption
fair_test_rationale: The crash is a slab freelist GPF in process creation, with no bpf frames. Getting from the poison value, the cache size and the freelist offset to the arena vma_list double close is a hard but fair diagnosis, and the crash gives no hint of the fix.

problems: The production_validation claim is false. There are 320 distinct hosts for MID e0c88670 and 305 for the arena_vm_close MID cce3695658b4759367800cdefbec18b9, but only 9 hosts appear in both, not 208 (checked with a distinct-hostname intersection in scuba_kernel_logview, ds >= 2025-10-06). The case relies on this fleet correlation as its main evidence, because the crash stack has no bpf frames.
The sample host od4223.cco2.facebook.com has no rows in the arena_vm_close MID cce36956. Nothing on the sample host itself ties this crash to bpf arena.

The start times are wrong. The first row for this MID is 1785177823 (2026-07-27 18:43 UTC), not 17:10. The arena MID starts at 1785174026 (17:40 UTC), not 16:07. The roughly 1-hour gap between them is still correct.

With the correlation gone, the only link to b90d77e5 is the poison arithmetic. That arithmetic is plausible: struct vma_list is 24 bytes, so it lives in kmalloc-32. The SLUB free pointer sits at offset 16, where list_del writes LIST_POISON2 (0xdead000000000122), and the fault address is that plus 0x10. SLAB_FREELIST_HARDENED, DEBUG_LIST and LIST_HARDENED are all unset in common.config, and the hardened flavor does not enable them. But any stale list_del or double free on a kmalloc-32 object would produce the same pattern, so this does not single out the arena bug, and the case cannot be called an exact_fix.

Checks that passed: the MID exists with the stated category_key and 1844 rows, all on 6.9.0 kernels, with none on 6.11 or later. The sample row od4223 at 1789625327 on 6.9.0-0_fbk12_hardened_0_g28f2d09ad102 exists. Fix b90d77e5 is by a human author (Alexei Starovoitov). It is on linus-upstream, v6.11-fb, v6.13-fb and v6.16-fb, and missing from v6.9-fb and from crash commit 28f2d09ad102. Its changelog (add a refcnt to stop use-after-free in arena_vm_close) matches the proposed root cause.

fix.subject: btrfs: replace writeback inhibition xarray with a fixed inline buffer
fix.author: Leo Martins
fix.landed_on: refs/heads/v6.16-fb (first in tag v6.16-fbk7-rc0); cherry-pick of upstream 7a433ed7fc22

signature_match_evidence: The crash is a soft lockup with btrfs_uninhibit_all_eb_writeback on top, called from btrfs_evict_inode -> iput/dput (sibling MIDs show xas_find/xa_find_after under the same function). The changelog says btrfs_uninhibit_all_eb_writeback() walks every inhibited eb with xa_for_each() in __btrfs_end_transaction() before num_writers drops. A single handle that COWs very many blocks, which it names as 'inode eviction, or truncate of a file with many extents', makes that walk arbitrarily long and causes multi-second stalls and RCU stall reports. The fix replaces the xarray with an 8-slot inline CLOCK array, so the cleanup walk is bounded.
production_validation: The fix is in v6.16-fbk7 and later. Every 6.16 kernel without it (fbk3/fbk4/fbk5/fbk6) hit uninhibit lockups (87/210/302/4 since 2026-07-01, counting sibling MIDs). This exact MID went quiet on fbk5/fbk6 only because a frame there is named evict instead of iput. fbk7/fbk702/fbk704/fbk8, which contain the fix, show 0 uninhibit crashes out of ~370 crashes of other MIDs. The sample is small because fbk7 is only starting to deploy.
gt_root_cause: Commit f9a48549a15a/0858a33c1390 ('btrfs: inhibit extent buffer writeback to prevent COW amplification') tracks every COWed eb in a per-transaction-handle xarray. btrfs_uninhibit_all_eb_writeback() iterates that whole xarray in __btrfs_end_transaction() without a bound. When btrfs_evict_inode()/btrfs_truncate_inode_items() COWs a huge number of tree blocks under one handle (evicting or truncating a heavily fragmented file), the walk runs for tens of seconds and triggers soft lockups and RCU stalls.
family_label: btrfs eb writeback-inhibit unbounded xarray walk on inode eviction
fair_test_rationale: The crash names btrfs_uninhibit_all_eb_writeback and the eviction path, but not the fix. To find it you have to see that the inhibition tracking structure (an xarray keyed per handle) grows without bound on large evictions, then find the later redesign to a bounded CLOCK buffer, whose title never mentions uninhibit, lockups or eviction. The crash kernel tag v6.16-fbk3-hotfix10 does not contain the fix (merge-base --is-ancestor fails).

problems: Minor provenance issue: the cherry-pick trailer names upstream commit 7a433ed7fc22358185a3b48e4bbe405c1cb083ad, but that object isn't in the mirror, so I couldn't confirm it landed upstream. The fix itself, 9d0732da23b9, is on refs/heads/v6.16-fb, and v6.16-fbk7-rc0, fbk7, fbk706 and fbk8-rc0 all contain it.

fix.subject: mm/huge_memory: fix dereferencing invalid pmd migration entry
fix.author: Gavin Guo
fix.landed_on: linus-upstream (v6.15-rc6); present in v6.16-fb, v6.19-fb, v7.1-fb; never backported to v6.13-fb

signature_match_evidence: The fleet panic is 'BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffea40xxxxx008' in split_huge_pmd_locked <- __split_huge_pmd <- try_to_migrate_one <- rmap_walk_anon <- try_to_migrate. The changelog's splat is 'BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffea60001db008' at RIP split_huge_pmd_locked, called from try_to_migrate_one <- rmap_walk_anon <- unmap_folio: the same vmemmap +0x8 fault. Cause: pmd_folio() is applied to a PMD migration entry, giving a bogus struct page. The v6.13-fb code (fbk18-rc1 and branch head) still has 'if (folio && folio != pmd_folio(*pmd)) return;' inside the is_pmd_migration_entry() branch, with no pmd_migration short-circuit.
production_validation: This MID has 184 crashes, all on 6.13 kernels (fbk7 through fbk18, still rising: 76 on fbk15). 6.16/7.1 kernels contain be6e843fc51a and have 0 crashes with the try_to_migrate_one->split_huge_pmd_locked signature since 2026-01-01, out of ~200k 6.16 crashes. 6.16 does have separate split_huge_pmd_locked crashes from zap/fault/mprotect paths where folio==NULL, which are a different bug that this fix does not cover.
gt_root_cause: THP migration races with the deferred-split (or other) rmap walk. try_to_migrate_one() calls split_huge_pmd_locked() with a folio on a PMD that another thread has already turned into a PMD migration entry. split_huge_pmd_locked() then calls pmd_folio(*pmd) on the swap-format entry, which yields a garbage pfn and struct page pointer, and the page-fault oops happens in the vmemmap area. Fix: return early when the PMD is a migration entry and a folio was passed, since a locked migration entry can never be the target folio.
family_label: THP split_huge_pmd_locked pmd_folio() on PMD migration entry
fair_test_rationale: The raw crash shows only split_huge_pmd_locked/try_to_migrate_one and a bad vmemmap address. To reach the fix you have to reason that the PMD is a migration entry being passed to pmd_folio(), then find an upstream mm fix that v6.13-fb never picked up. The fix title does not name any stack function. The crash kernel commit 4c0a55d54424 (v6.13-fbk18-rc1) is not a descendant of be6e843fc51a, and v6.13-fb head still has the buggy code.

problems: Small count drift, not a real problem: since ds>=2025-10-06 the MID now shows 185 rows on 181 distinct hosts (the case says 184 crashes on 180 hosts). The MID is still getting new crashes, so this is expected. Every row has the one category_key, and the rows run from 1762867359 to 1790797197.

fix.subject: btrfs: fix subpage nullptr dereference
fix.author: Boris Burkov
fix.landed_on: refs/heads/v6.13-fb (tip of v6.13-fbk5; merged via 'subpage-eb-null-6.13', cherry-pick of Meta commit 5b57fd494b52)

signature_match_evidence: This is arm64 (64K pages, so the btrfs subpage path): 'Unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at virtual address 0000000000000000' in btree_write_cache_pages (submit_eb_subpage is inlined into it) during writeback. The fix changes submit_eb_subpage(), which read subpage = folio_get_private(folio) outside mapping->i_private_lock and only then checked folio_test_private() under the lock. Per the changelog: 'The subpage is cleared under the mapping->i_private_lock but we access it outside the lock... does not rule out the possibility of a race.' The fix loads the pointer under the lock and NULL-checks it. A concurrent release that clears folio private leaves a NULL subpage to be dereferenced, which is exactly this crash.
production_validation: This MID appears only on kernels without the fix: 6.11 fbk7/11/12/13 (the 6.11 backport bd1ccf323210 never reached a release tag), 6.13 fbk0/1/3/4, and 6.13-fbk5-rc0. 6.13-fbk5 final and every later 6.13 release contain cfc0605e4628 and have 0 crashes of this MID since 2025-10-06. Those kernels logged roughly 10k other arm64-style crashes, so arm64 hosts were running them. 6.13-fbk4 hosts without the fix kept crashing through Aug 2026.
gt_root_cause: In the btrfs subpage (sectorsize < PAGE_SIZE, e.g. arm64 64K pages) metadata writeback path, submit_eb_subpage() read folio private (the btrfs_subpage pointer) without holding mapping->i_private_lock. A concurrent folio release/detach can clear folio private under that lock. The loop then uses a NULL (or stale) subpage pointer to scan the dirty bitmap, and a NULL pointer dereference follows in btree_write_cache_pages().
family_label: btrfs subpage eb writeback NULL folio private race
fair_test_rationale: The crash shows only btree_write_cache_pages/btree_writepages and a NULL deref on arm64. To reach the fix you have to infer the inlined submit_eb_subpage and the unlocked folio_get_private() read. The fix title does not name any stack frame. The sample crash kernel (g81eeacf23a9f, v6.13-fbk4) lacks the fix. Caveat: 6.13-fbk5 kernels' uname contains the fix sha cfc0605e4628 itself, so samples should come from fbk4 or older and never from fbk5 kernels.

problems: The fix.sha field is wrong: cfc0605e46286adbd0d1c6ddcde45eed8359e1d8 is not an object in the mirror ('bad object'). The real full SHA is cfc0605e4628bd450988e9c9032ee652afd4dfb3. The 12-char prefix cfc0605e4628 is correct, and subject, author and date match.

Everything else checks out. The fix is an ancestor of refs/heads/v6.13-fb. Its author is Boris Burkov (a human), and it is a cherry-pick of 5b57fd494b52. The changelog and diff match: the folio_get_private() read moves under i_private_lock in submit_eb_subpage and gets a NULL check. Crash kernel 81eeacf23a9f (Release 6.13-fbk4) does not contain the fix. The sample row exists in scuba_kernel_logview with the stated host, time, kernel and category_key.
